subsystems.name: Cartridge and ingredient feed
subsystems.role: stores and delivers the edible pastes and nutrient concentrates that get printed.

subsystems.name: Print head
subsystems.role: deposits material in controlled droplets or extruded lines to build up a dish layer by layer.

subsystems.name: Rheology control
subsystems.role: keeps every paste printable and keeps the finished dish from collapsing.

subsystems.name: Nutrition model
subsystems.role: decides what the dish should contain, based on the user's data.

subsystems.name: Inline sensing and metering
subsystems.role: verifies that the printed portion actually contains the intended amounts.

subsystems.name: Finishing module
subsystems.role: cooks, sets or textures the printed item so it is edible.
parts: laser or heated roller for browning

subsystems.name: Hygiene and safety system
subsystems.role: keeps a warm, wet, nutrient-rich machine from becoming a microbiological hazard.

buildSteps.title: Formulate printable pastes
buildSteps.detail: Real ingredients are blended and adjusted with gelling and thickening agents until they flow through a nozzle but hold their shape once deposited — the same rheology principles used in spherification and gel-based molecular gastronomy.

buildSteps.title: Prepare nutrient concentrates
buildSteps.detail: Vitamins, minerals, amino acids and fatty acids are supplied as food-grade powders or oils, dissolved or encapsulated, and dosed so a printed portion delivers a defined fraction of a daily requirement.

buildSteps.title: Build the deposition hardware
buildSteps.detail: Nozzles, pumps and a multi-axis gantry are assembled so several materials can be laid down in one item, with droplet or line widths from a fraction of a millimetre upward.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop with sensing
buildSteps.detail: Mass-flow, pressure and camera feedback detect clogged nozzles and under-dosing, and let the machine correct mid-print rather than trusting an open-loop recipe.

buildSteps.title: Connect the nutrition model
buildSteps.detail: User data — intake records, wearables and periodic blood tests for markers such as ferritin or vitamin D — feed an algorithm that converts a calculated shortfall into a target nutrient mix for the next meal.

buildSteps.title: Add cooking and finishing
buildSteps.detail: Heat or chilling is applied during or after printing to set gels, cook proteins and create texture, since nutrients and food safety both depend on temperature history.

buildSteps.title: Validate food safety
buildSteps.detail: Cleaning cycles, allergen changeover and shelf-life are tested against food-safety rules before any machine goes into a kitchen or clinic.

buildSteps.title: Run controlled feeding studies
buildSteps.detail: Only a trial measuring biomarkers over months can show whether printed personalised meals actually change nutritional status.

prerequisites.why: extrusion food printers exist commercially, but multi-material printing at nutrient-level precision is still laboratory work.
many vitamins taste bitter or degrade in air, so they must be coated before they can sit in a cartridge.
glucose can be tracked under the skin in real time, but iron, vitamin D, B12 and most other nutrients still need a blood draw — so 'real-time deficit' cannot yet be measured.
responses to diet vary between people, but the field cannot yet predict an individual's exact requirement.
standard hygiene, allergen and temperature controls already apply and would simply need to be engineered into the machine.

pathway.milestone: single- and multi-material food printers used by chefs and in some care settings
pathway.unlocks: textured, swallow-friendly purees for people with chewing or swallowing difficulty.

pathway.milestone: printers that meet a nutrient prescription set by a dietitian
pathway.unlocks: hospital and aged-care meals with verified, reproducible composition.

pathway.milestone: cheap biomarker panels or reliable wearable nutrient sensing
pathway.unlocks: closing the loop — measuring a shortfall and printing against it without a clinic visit.

pathway.milestone: validated trials linking printed personalised meals to health outcomes
pathway.unlocks: a plausible consumer or clinical product, and a clearer picture of how much personalisation actually helps.
